# OSHA Confined Space Awareness Training

> 3-hour online awareness-level course on OSHA's Confined Spaces in Construction standard, 29 CFR 1926 Subpart AA. Available in English and Spanish. Offered by HAZWOPER OSHA Training (https://hazwoper-osha.com).

## Key facts
- Duration: 3 hours; 6 lessons, final exam
- Credits: 0.3 CEU
- Price: $49.99 per person; bulk pricing available
- Delivery: 100% online, 24/7, audio playback; SCORM, virtual and on-site formats also available
- Languages: English, Spanish
- Prerequisites: none
- Certificate: downloadable on passing; valid 3 years
- Scope: awareness only; does not qualify employees to enter confined spaces

## What makes a space confined (OSHA)
1. Large enough and configured so a worker can fully enter it
2. Limited or restricted means of entry or exit
3. Not designed for continuous occupancy

## Permit-required conditions (29 CFR 1926.1202)
- Contains or may contain a hazardous atmosphere
- Contains material that could engulf an entrant
- Internal configuration that could trap or asphyxiate an entrant
- Contains any other recognized serious safety or health hazard

## Lessons
1. What Is a Confined Space? (criteria, permit-required conditions, entrant/attendant/supervisor roles)
2. Confined Space Hazards (flammable, toxic, oxygen-deficient atmospheres; engulfment and other physical hazards)
3. Regulatory Requirements (reclassification, alternate entry procedures, ventilation)
4. Confined Spaces Program (permit-required programs, entry permits, documentation, training)
5. Hazard Controls and Safety Precautions (hierarchy of controls, air testing, purging, ventilation, energy isolation)
6. Rescue and Emergency Procedures (medical emergencies, three types of rescue, retrieval systems, rescue teams)

## Who should take it
Construction workers around pits, manholes, crawl spaces, vaults or tanks; entrants, attendants and entry supervisors; maintenance workers, electricians, plumbers and HVAC technicians; utility, pipeline and underground crews; contractors, project managers and site safety managers; emergency response personnel.
